verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'Pacific Ocean, off the coast of San Diego, California'; R4: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'raft in the Pacific Ocean... 60 miles off San Diego'; R6: 'off the coast of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the splashdown location as Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: '8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 PDT... April 10, 2026'; R3: '8:07 p.m. Eastern Stanard Time... April 10'; R4: '8:07 p.m. ET'; R5: '8:07 p.m. EDT'; R6: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm the exact time and date of splashdown, with articles dated April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II flight lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: mission began April 1, splashdown April 10 (10-day span); R2: 'historic 10-day mission'; R3: '10-day mission first began April 1'; R4: '10-day journey... 10-day mission'; R5: 'nearly 10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe the mission as a 10-day mission, matching launch on April 1 and splashdown on April 10.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II flight took the crew around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'human spaceflight around the moon... swung around the moon’s far side'; R2: 'moon mission to the moon and back'; R3: 'trip around the moon'; R4: 'journey around the moon and back'; R5: 'mission around the Moon'; R6: implies lunar mission context
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly describe the mission as going around the Moon and returning to Earth.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule reached speeds of approximately 25,000 mph upon re-entry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'more than 24,000 miles per hour... peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour'; R2: 'speeds up to 25,000 mph... peak velocity of 24,664 miles per hour... estimated at 25,000 mph'; R4: '24,664 miles per hour'; R5: 'nearly 25,000 mph... roughly 24,000 miles per hour'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm re-entry speeds around 24,000-25,000 mph, with exact peak of 24,664 mph, supporting 'approximately 25,000 mph'.

verifications.claim: NASA recovery teams were stationed in the Pacific to retrieve Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team... off San Diego... Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'; R2: 'Navy dive team... Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen... USS John P. Murtha'; similar crew lists and recovery in Pacific across R3-R6
verifications.reasoning: Sources name the exact crew and describe NASA/Navy recovery teams stationed in the Pacific Ocean for retrieval.

verifications.claim: The splashdown occurred west of San Diego.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'waters off San Diego' (Pacific); R2: 'off the coast of San Diego... West Coast'; R3: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'; R4: 'off California’s coast... off the coast of San Diego'; R5: '60 miles off San Diego' (Pacific)
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify 'off the coast of San Diego in the Pacific,' which geographically is west, but do not explicitly state 'west of San Diego'; supported but less precise.
